unresolved.name: Forte Digital
unresolved.question: Is the listed Zurich technical operation current?

evidence.finding: Official indexed July 2024 announcement identifies an employee app for Migros Aare; direct retrieval failed, primary indexed text was readable.
Official account identifies Berlin-based Central Europe delivery for Migros.
Current office roster lists Norway, Poland, Germany and Denmark, but not Zurich. Omission is a verification gap, not proof of closure.
Current Berlin product role supports continuing development, but not a Swiss development location.

unresolved.reason: Official 1 August 2024 leadership announcement explicitly says offices had recently opened in Switzerland and Austria. This is affirmative historical Swiss-office evidence, stronger than a Swiss customer reference. Current office list still omits Switzerland; no closure proof or current Zurich occupancy identified.
unresolved.limitation: Does Forte currently maintain the listed Zurich office/team, and at which address?

unresolved.name: icentic
unresolved.question: Does current icentic contribute to beppo or another maintained original technology?

evidence.finding: Current account describes incubation of digital spin-offs and shared founder/leadership with beppo.
Beppo identifies itself as an icentic spin-off and says its Zurich headquarters continues developing parking/fuel-theft tools.
Current catalogue includes turnkey software as well as staff/teams and development-centre setup; no named current icentic-owned platform branch.
Co-development and complete software work packages are substantive, but current contribution to the identified original platform remains unconfirmed.

unresolved.reason: Current company catalogue expressly offers joint or commissioned development of modules/platforms. Beppo's own current account identifies its icentic origin and continued Zurich development, but not current icentic participation. This is substantive software work, not merely support; founder overlap alone does not attribute the separate spin-off's technology.
unresolved.limitation: Does current icentic continue developing beppo or another company-originated technology, beyond client-only development assignments?

unresolved.name: KOCH IT
unresolved.question: How should the absorbed entity and unconfirmed Winterthur office be represented under Adnovum?

evidence.finding: 20 May 2026 announcement says the Koch IT absorption merger completed in April and incorporated its team into Adnovum public sector. Corrects earlier loose May-integration wording.
Current Swiss locations include Zurich, Bern and Lausanne; no Winterthur match.

unresolved.reason: Adnovum's dated announcement confirms April 2026 absorption into its public-sector team. Its current contact roster does not list Winterthur. The technical business continues through the successor; the unresolved issue is representation of the predecessor and its location, not technical eligibility.
unresolved.limitation: Should the existing Koch profile be represented as an Adnovum predecessor/site, and is the Winterthur location still occupied?

unresolved.name: Mathys Partner
unresolved.question: Does Mathys develop the simulation software or original computational methods rather than solely apply external tools?

evidence.finding: Specialist simulation practice and technical methods; not explicit software authorship.
BFE October 2024 report, printed page 43: Mathys can calculate and visualise glare; unlike adjacent entries, no explicit development history is given.

unresolved.reason: Simulation.solar documents specialist optical computation, methodological criticism and ongoing interdisciplinary work. Direct reads recover visualisierung.ch as a Mathys page linking simulation.solar; glarecontrol.aero is an image-only placeholder, not evidence of a launched software product. Neither fact establishes or disproves original simulation-method development.
unresolved.limitation: Which simulation method, computational component or technical process does Mathys itself develop rather than only apply?

unresolved.name: mecas
unresolved.question: What concrete technical work can be attributed to Mecas?

evidence.finding: Current physical-AI research claims; no named output on homepage.

unresolved.reason: Current first-party imprint confirms Mecas GmbH, Zurich address and leadership. Founder-authored hiring post describes building production AI systems; company page describes vision, sensor processing and robotics. The linked Notion careers page returns 404. These establish a technical team and local identity, but do not distinguish own/joint technology from client-only projects.
unresolved.limitation: What concrete original or jointly developed system/method can be attributed to Mecas beyond commissioned implementation?

unresolved.limitation: Does walkingtoweb itself contribute original continuing blue.project development, jointly with walkingtoyou, or only host and sell it?

withdrawn.reason: Digital Unit, explicitly Stutz's offering, maintains Gaia Core as a common headless platform across several product tiers and implementations, with extension, intelligence and care modules. This is concrete reusable maintained software, not a requirement to invent the underlying CMS. Sanity remains the upstream CMS; its native collaboration features are not credited as Stutz inventions.

Withdraw the exclusion recommendation: the current official support page explicitly attributes a from-scratch rebuild of its customer portal, with live service management, tickets, requests and billing. Concrete original maintained software is supported. VMware, cloudscale and Anapaya remain upstream vendors; no invention of their technology is inferred.

Withdraw the service-only exclusion: the specific medicinal-cannabis case says the company initiated development and successfully developed several stable marketed formulations. Original formulation/process development qualifies without patents or a standalone branded platform. The separate inhalation device remains a client collaboration, not credited as wholly Trias-owned.

SmartCampus explicitly undergoes continuing CrossWorks development, confirmed by its customer account of the original solution being continued and professionalised. All named product branches were checked: HS/SA is a multi-canton roadtraffic application; SwissContentCloud is an IBM-based DMS offering; KIM remains third-party CRM and does not determine company eligibility.

Official company history explicitly states that development of Swiss Private Cloud uNimbus began in 2025. Green hosting, IBM infrastructure and SolarWinds-powered UniVision do not disprove original uNimbus development. The catalogue does not identify an original control-plane/software component or technical process. Prior exclusion is unsafe until this branch is resolved.

WITHDRAW: catalogue alone missed Asbera. Official product site offers maintained web/mobile SaaS for hazardous-building-material surveys; its legal notice identifies the exact Zurich Blackpoints entity. Developer-authored Google Play listing identifies Blackpoints AG and an August 2026 technology update. This is concrete own product development, not merely iGovPortal/Inventsys resale.

Current official WordPress offering explicitly lists custom-developed plugins used for tracking updates and maintenance. Together with detailed original ACF/Timber mapping, field caching and recursion-handling work, this supports continuing company-developed tooling, not merely installing WordPress. No separate marketed product or recent public commit is required.

evidence.finding: Current FAQ lists custom-developed plugins for tracking updates and maintenance; service description includes continuing development.
2018 technical account attributes automatic field mapping, caching and recursion handling to its own engineers; historical corroboration, not a fresh maintenance claim.

recommendations.name: webunique
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Agency delivery workflow describes client websites/apps and customer handover; Camply/Dalia are customer references.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Read homepage service navigation, named Camply/Dalia references and delivery/acceptance/handover workflow. Product search yielded no attributable separate branch; conclusion rests on the affirmative agency catalogue, not search absence.

recommendations.name: BeeBase
recommendations.strongestEvidence: AI service uses third-party Langdock; remaining catalogue is client setup, training and outsourced IT operation.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Checked both published service divisions and FAQ: outsourced IT operation plus AI setup/training. Named platform is Langdock, with BeeBase explicitly responsible for configuration and workflow integration.

recommendations.name: Citrus
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Company history explicitly focuses on Google Workspace/Cloud rollout, maintenance, integration and training.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Company remit expressly covers Google Workspace/Cloud rollout, maintenance and support plus selected vendor tools. Catalogue and team roles corroborate deployment/training; no named original product branch surfaced.

recommendations.name: Consys
recommendations.strongestEvidence: History selects AAC Infotray's Limsophy; catalogue describes distribution, configuration and regulatory consulting.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Reviewed current full QM software modules and monday.com branch against prior history/fusion/customer evidence. Product branding alone is misleading: history assigns Limsophy to AAC Infotray; hyperManager supplier material assigns its development to Scheuring. Consultancy, introduction and configuration remain the published Consys role.

recommendations.name: creative matters
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Client product-design agency; showcased 9T Labs printer belongs to the customer, not the agency.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Current full catalogue separates strategy, innovation workshops and industrial/UI design, mockups and implementation support. Portfolio explicitly groups projects by customers including 9T Labs, Hemotune and Securiton. No company-owned technology branch identified; not a claim that their design work is trivial.

recommendations.name: Data Purpose
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Published packages sell SAP/Microsoft architecture reviews, proofs of concept, dashboards and training.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Read base packages and additional AI branch: architecture reviews, vendor-tenant setup, use-case prototypes, training and engineer residency. AI packages are time-bounded consultancy using SAP/Microsoft or model access, not a named maintained company platform.

recommendations.name: Digitalmaterial
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Automation explicitly uses Endpoint Manager, Intune, Entra ID and Defender to provision customer equipment.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Reviewed current infrastructure/support/M365 catalogue, automation and company history. Current business describes operating customer IT with manufacturer partnerships; old shared-group software terms do not establish a Digitalmaterial product.

recommendations.name: evolyze GmbH
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Project catalogue describes client implementations; databaum case improves the customer's existing ML model.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Reviewed current consulting and implementation catalogue, projects and company-submitted software-directory entry. Named databaum/Vatorex/Cotra work is customer engineering; directory offering is Software Development Services & Consulting, not an identified original product. This is a scope recommendation under client-only criteria, not a no-engineering claim.

recommendations.name: Helvetic IT Solution
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Catalogue offers managed vendor ICT and commissioned websites/software; calculators are assessment aids.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Read full catalogue including easily missed Software Development and Tools branches. Development is commissioned websites/apps/internal customer tools; published self-assessments and downtime calculator are simple advisory aids. Managed ICT remains vendor-based; no substantive company platform is established.

recommendations.name: incendia
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Catalogue begins with SAP standard functionality and customer-specific interfaces, forms, extensions and support.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Full service page explicitly describes customer-specific applications, SAP extensions, ABAP interfaces/forms, project management and ongoing support. Original coding is acknowledged; no claim is made that SAP use itself disqualifies. Published offering remains client-only customisation rather than an identified maintained company technology branch.

recommendations.name: Intecso
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Full catalogue describes Azure/M365/Copilot, monitoring, migration and customer support; main independently agrees.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Current full service navigation covers service desk, consulting, modern work, backup, security, Zero Trust, Azure migration/operation, Copilot enablement and monitoring. Product-branch search did not add contradictory evidence. The recommendation relies on that explicit managed-ICT catalogue.

recommendations.name: ITIVITY
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Service catalogue and Grob Kies case describe standard-technology managed infrastructure and pay-per-use operation.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Direct current catalogue fetch succeeds: modular cloud, cybersecurity, Microsoft, backup and SLA/support. Reused Grob Kies actual-delivery case corroborates standard-infrastructure migration and operation. Unrelated iTivity software businesses were rejected as identity mismatches.

recommendations.name: Nomasis
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Catalogue/history and engineer duties centre on third-party MDM/MTD rollout, configuration and operation.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Checked platform/service catalogue, company history, engineering and EMEA branch. EMEA includes broad software-development language but identifies no Nomasis original system; concrete engineer/service descriptions remain rollout and management of vendor mobile platforms.

recommendations.name: onmit
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Software catalogue is commissioned delivery; Teacher Switch is explicitly built for a separate startup using Twilio.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Full catalogue includes network/cloud management, web design and individual web applications. Reviewed named customer references and published service terms; Teacher Switch is a separate startup's application. No company product branch was evidenced; not excluded merely because it uses Twilio or OSS.

recommendations.name: Pront
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Named Interdiscount/Helsana cases concern migration, DevOps and architecture/operating-model consulting.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Reviewed projects plus Data & AI branch, not merely the cloud partner relationship. Interdiscount case is migration/DevOps and Helsana case is strategy/architecture; service branches offer advisory and implementation work rather than an attributed platform.

recommendations.name: relyz
recommendations.strongestEvidence: Published delivery workflow is client websites, CRM/content hubs, LLM integration and marketing automation.
recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Read entire service navigation, current AI offering and named KI-Kompass branch. KI-Kompass is a strategy/maturity method, not an original software platform. AI services centre on training, governance and customer API/MCP integration; current case catalogue remains client delivery.

recommendations.name: Swiss Infosec

recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Expanded beyond SwissGRC: checked consulting, mandates, awareness, eLearning and Academy. Original SCORM training content is acknowledged; Academy explicitly uses easylearn's LMS and hosting. GRC software is separately attributed to Swiss GRC. No original security/software platform established across these branches.

recommendations.name: WOn-Data

recommendations.finalCatalogueReview: Direct full service catalogue covers colocation, power, cooling, connectivity and operations. Reporting portal is mentioned but no original development attributed. This remains infrastructure operation under the company criterion, not a claim of inactivity or unskilled work.
